Daily Economic Briefing

Monday, 27 July 2026

Durable Goods 08:30 ETTreasury 11:30 / 13:00FOMC Tomorrow
Liquidity & Stress Metrics - The Gnosis Pulse
MOVE is Treasury volatility and term-premium stress; SOFR is secured overnight funding; NFCI is broad financial conditions, where negative readings indicate looser conditions and positive readings indicate tighter conditions. Today's scheduled impulse is more about rate-supply digestion than a broad data slate.
Gnosis Interpretation
Durable goods can move the growth/capex narrative before the cash open. Treasury auctions then test demand across bills and the 2-year/5-year sector ahead of the July 28-29 FOMC meeting.
Economic Calendar: 2026-07-27
Primary-source conflict check passed. BLS, BEA, Census, EIA, TreasuryDirect/FiscalData, Federal Reserve, EIA, and NYSE/CME market-structure calendars were checked. No Investing.com, market-calendar aggregator, Google Drive, or Google Docs source was used.

Omissions and Watch
BLS and BEA showed no material date-specific release for 27 July. EIA's next major weekly energy reports are later in the week, not today. No NYSE holiday or shortened session was verified for today, and no standard equity-index options expiry falls on 27 July. The Federal Reserve's July FOMC meeting is verified for 28-29 July, so today is positioning and pre-FOMC risk rather than a decision day.
Trading Strategy Note (ES Futures)
Base case: Let 08:30 durable goods define the first growth impulse, then watch Treasury auction tails and front-end yields for confirmation before leaning into directional ES trades.
Invalidation: If rates absorb supply cleanly and no verified policy headline appears, avoid over-weighting pre-FOMC fear. If auction demand is weak, treat it as a rates-volatility risk signal rather than a standalone equity signal.
